title: aid-service-declaration/1
description: The shape of the OPTIONAL `services:` map in a project's execution.yaml — the per-project declaration of long-lived processes a run may need standing up (a database, a dev server, a queue). AID starts nothing on its own authority: a project that declares no services keeps byte-identical runner behaviour, and the shipped template ships this block as commentary with zero active services. This file is the DOCUMENTATION + test authority for the shape; the RUNTIME enforcement is `_validate_services_config` in scripts/aid-run-gates.sh, which mirrors every constraint below and runs at `run_all` entry, before any service or gate action. The two are held together by the shared fixture set in scripts/tests/bats/test-service-declaration.bats, which drives BOTH from the same case table — if one drifts, that suite fails.

propertyNames.description: Service names are lowercase identifiers: they end up in log lines, job directory names and error messages, so they stay filesystem- and shell-safe.

start_cmd.description: The command that starts the service. It MUST remain the foreground process of its job — no `&`, no `nohup`, no self-daemonising fork. The supervisor owns the process group; a command that backgrounds itself hands back a pid that owns nothing, and the run loses the ability to stop what it started. That MUST is now partly checked rather than merely stated, and the limit of the check is stated with it: the two `not`/`pattern` clauses below are a SYNTACTIC lint that refuses the obvious backgrounding forms — a trailing `&` (a trailing `&&` is not one), and `nohup`, `disown` or `setsid` used as a command word. It cannot see a command that daemonises INSIDE itself (`npm start` invoking a wrapper that forks and exits, a `docker run -d` hidden behind a script). That residual case is not left uncovered, it is simply not coverable here: it is caught at runtime, by the rule that a TERMINAL job whose probe still reports healthy is a daemonised start_cmd. Treat a clean validation as 'no obvious backgrounding syntax', never as 'proven foreground'.

allOf.$comment: No trailing `&`. `(^|[^&])&\s*$` deliberately lets a trailing `&&` through — that is a syntax error for the shell to reject, not a backgrounding form.
No `nohup` / `disown` / `setsid` as a command word (start of string, or after whitespace, `;`, `&`, `|` or `(`).

probe_cmd.description: The health probe. Exit 0 means healthy; any other exit means not yet (or no longer) healthy. It is polled, so it must be cheap and side-effect free.

startup_deadline_seconds.description: The HEALTH-PROBE budget only: absent -> starting must reach healthy within this many seconds, or the service is declared failed to start. Deliberately NOT the process lifetime — see max_lifetime_seconds.

max_lifetime_seconds.description: The aid-job whole-process deadline — a run-lifetime ceiling, kept SEPARATE from startup_deadline_seconds so one number never has to mean both 'how long may it take to come up' and 'how long may it live'. Default 86400 (24 h).

stop_cmd.description: Graceful shutdown command. Optional: when absent, teardown relies on job cancel alone (process-group kill), which is acceptable for a process with no external state to flush.

log_hint.description: Where this service's own logs land (a path, a container name, a docker logs invocation) — surfaced to a human diagnosing a failed startup. Free-form prose, read by nobody but a person.

restart_authorized.description: Whether an automated run may restart this service after it dies. Defaults to FALSE: repairs are opt-in authority, never assumed.

port_env.description: Name of the environment variable that carries the per-run allocated port. OPTIONAL, and its absence is the honestly-named shared-resource escape hatch: a service on a fixed external port (an existing shared database) declares no port_env and port allocation is skipped for it. Two services may never name the SAME port_env — one env var, one owner. That uniqueness constraint is not expressible in JSON Schema across sibling properties; it is enforced by _validate_services_config and covered by the shared fixture set. Beyond being a legal env var name, the name is DENIED if it is one the runner's own children depend on: this variable is exported into the environment of every service and gate command, so `port_env: PATH` would set PATH to a port number for the whole run, and `port_env: BASH_ENV` or `LD_PRELOAD` would point a code-loading hook at one. The denylist below is grouped by what the variable controls — command lookup, shell parsing and startup, interpreter/loader hooks, git's own exec hooks, and AID's runtime state (the `AID_` prefix). Matching is EXACT and CASE-SENSITIVE for the enumerated names, and case-sensitive PREFIX for the open-ended loader/function families (`LD_`, `DYLD_`, `BASH_FUNC_`, `AID_`). Case-sensitive because environment variables are: `Path` is not `PATH` and no loader, shell or interpreter honours it, so refusing the case variant would cost a false refusal and buy nothing. Prefix only where the family is genuinely open-ended and libc/shell-version dependent, so an enumeration would silently go stale.

allOf.$comment: Exact, case-sensitive denials. Kept in the same order as the runtime denylist in _validate_services_config.
Case-sensitive prefix denials for the open-ended families: the dynamic loaders (LD_*, DYLD_*), bash's exported-function smuggling channel (BASH_FUNC_*) and AID's own runtime namespace (AID_*).
